title: Passage Lumen: Workspace Signal & Route Reframe
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary: Reframe the Console left navigation and workspace switching experience to improve discoverability of dashboards, rollout controls, and cost lenses while keeping density low for power users. The ‘Passage Lumen’ concept introduces a signal-driven compact rail plus a lightweight workspace chip strip to surface context-sensitive routes (dashboards, rollouts, cost views) without increasing cognitive load.

Goals:
- Reduce average time-to-open key surfaces (Dashboard, Rollouts, Cost Breakdown) by 25% in quick-access flows.
- Make workspace switching visible and role-aware (owner, viewer) with minimal clicks.
- Surface cost-impact signals inline in navigation (token cost badge, recent anomalies) without noisy UI.

Scope:
- IA changes for left rail + top chip strip (workspace).
- Component prototypes for: compact rail, workspace signal chips, route badges, and contextual flyouts for rollouts and cost previews.
- Handoff kit for engineering with spacing tokens, accessibility states, and motion spec.

Non-Goals:
- Full redesign of dashboard internals or Console theming.
- Backend routing or RBAC changes (engineering will adapt to existing APIs).

Acceptance criteria:
- Prototype v2 validated in unmoderated testing with 12 participants showing median time improvement vs control.
- Design tokens and component spec delivered (Figma + tokens.json export).
- Accessibility: keyboard navigable shortcuts, ARIA labels for workspace chips and route badges.
- PM sign-off on rollout preview flyout copy and telemetry hooks.

Design notes & tradeoffs:
- Compact rail vs hidden command palette: choose compact rail to reduce muscle-memory friction for teams who use Console frequently; command palette remains as fallback for power search.
- Signal badges (cost anomaly / high-latency routes) should be color-muted and optional per workspace to avoid alert fatigue.
- Workspace chip strip placed above the main content to avoid long vertical jumps; chips collapse to an overflow menu when >7 workspaces.
- Motion: use low-cost easing (80ms) for chip transitions to preserve perceived speed.

Deliverables:
- Figma prototypes: v1 static, v2 interactive (compact rail + chips), v3 edge case flows (many workspaces, long route names).
- Handoff doc (design-to-dev) with tokens, accessibility checklist, and telemetry key suggestions.
- User-testing plan + scripts for unmoderated A/B.

Success metrics:
- Time to open Dashboard/Rollouts/Cost view.
- Rate of workspace-switch per session.
- Reduction in support tickets referencing "can’t find dashboard".

Next steps:
1) Run internal design critique (complete).
2) Build interactive prototype v2 and ship to unmoderated testing (in progress).
3) Iterate on copy and microcopy per PM feedback; prepare engineering handoff after test results.

Notes for engineering:
- Provide hooks for optional cost badges controlled by server-side preferences.
- Route identifiers must be stable slugs for analytics (send route_slug in nav_click events).
- Keep left rail width configurable to allow dedicated deployments to pin density settings.
